entries.title: Add ChurchillFriction, one friction model valid across every flow regime
entries.body:
The friction models (`SwameeJainFriction`, `HaalandFriction`, `ColebrookFriction`) cover turbulent flow only.

## Expected

- `ChurchillFriction : IFrictionModel` in `src/LymCsharp.Hydraulics` implements Churchill's 1977 equation, valid for laminar, transitional and turbulent flow.
- Tests check it against `64/Re` in laminar flow and against `ColebrookFriction` within 1 % in turbulent flow.
- `RegressionCases` gains one case that runs a pipe flow through `ChurchillFriction`; the existing cases are unchanged.

## Why

This run proves how Drift treats a new regression case that the baseline does not hold, while every existing case stays clean.

entries.title: The pipe flow report prints its values to 4 significant digits
entries.body:
`ResultFormatter` (`src/LymCsharp.Reporting/ResultFormatter.cs`) formats the pipe flow report's numbers.

## Expected

- The report prints every numeric value to 4 significant digits.
- The formatter's tests follow the new format.
- The regression cases that render the formatted report now drift on purpose, and the run records that drift as intended.

## Why

This run proves that Drift reports an intended output change and that the run's Drift verify accepts it with a stated reason, on a hub whose anchor is `dotnet/`.
